## Rollout: env vars and secrets (ticket Scope, plan T9)

Reuse is OFF until all three of the first rows below are set. If any one is unset, `bin/ci-plan.sh` prints `reuse: off: no credential`, the record step prints `suite-reuse: record skipped (no credential)`, and every suite runs as it does today. Nothing breaks.

| name | kind | where it must be set | environments | read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SUITE_LEDGER_TOKEN` | GitHub Actions **secret** | `example-org/cromford` repo secrets | the one CI (no dev/staging split for this repo) | `harness-ci.yml` plan job env and `record suite results` step env; `harness-nightly.yml` record step env. Only on `push` or a `mergify/merge-queue/*` head ref (nightly: only on `schedule`); every other event gets `''` |
| `SUITE_LEDGER_URL` | GitHub Actions **repo variable** | `example-org/cromford` repo variables | same | the same three places; the jobs worker base URL |
| `SUITE_LEDGER_TOKEN` | Cloudflare **worker secret** | jobs worker (`worker/jobs`), `wrangler secret put SUITE_LEDGER_TOKEN` | the production worker the URL above points at | `worker/jobs/src/lib/suite-results.js` (`credentialClass`), from #5420. Same value as the GitHub secret |
| `CI_RUNNER` | GitHub Actions repo variable (already exists, optional) | repo variables | same | `CI_REUSE_CTX`; unset falls back to `"ubuntu-latest"`, the same default as `runs-on` (A4) |

Set inside the workflow only, never by hand: `CI_PLAN_REUSE: '1'`, `CI_REUSE_CTX`, `CI_PLAN_REUSE_DIR`, and `CI_PLAN_REUSED_FILE` (shard side, from the `suite-reuse-plan` artifact).

The knobs `SUITE_REUSE` (on/off) and `SUITE_REUSE_MAX_AGE_H` are the contract's DB settings rows (`lib.suite-reuse.*`, #5420). This PR adds none.

Order:
1. Merge #5420 and apply its D1 migration.
2. Put the worker secret.
3. Set the repo variable and the GitHub secret.

The first merge-queue batch after this PR merges runs every suite. `bin/ci-plan.sh` and the workflows are fingerprint inputs, so every fingerprint moves once. Reuse starts on the batches after that, once CI has recorded rows.

Proof rung: BUILT. No live probe of the ledger ran, because CI holds no token yet. The first real proof is a batch log with a `reuse: on ... reused N` line and `suite_results` rows carrying that run id.

## Residual trust risk (plan edge cases)

A member PR's code runs inside the merge-queue batch, and the batch's `record suite results` step holds the ledger token. A malicious or broken member PR could therefore write forged `ci` rows ("suite X passed for fingerprint F").

What bounds it:
- A fingerprint covers the suite's inputs AND the infra hash (workflows, `catalog/`, `tests/lib/`, the reuse code). A forged row only matches trees that carry the same inputs, so a PR that edits the reuse path moves every fingerprint and cannot forge rows for the unchanged tree.
- Every row carries `run_id` and `head_sha`, so a forged row traces back to the batch that wrote it.
- Ordinary PR runs get no token (`''`), so only code that a reviewer approved into the merge queue ever runs with it.

What stays: the trust boundary is the same as today's CI. Code that reaches the merge queue can already turn its own CI green. This PR adds no new privilege, but it extends the reach of a green to later batches with the same fingerprints. Turning reuse off is one row (`lib.suite-reuse.suite_reuse = off`) or unsetting the secret.

## I1: the builder -> batch repeat remains

This slice removes repeats between CI runs only (batch after batch, push-to-main corpus). It does NOT remove the repeat between the builder's own suite run on the build box and the merge-queue batch. The CI plan asks the ledger with `--class ci`, and the worker answers a CI-token lookup with `ci` rows only, so a `class builder` row never satisfies CI. That is deliberate (I1): a build box is not a trusted runner. The builder gate in sibling #5367 is the place that reuses builder-side results.

## Assumptions

The ticket did not settle these; the plan took the most conservative reading and built. Correct any of them here and the fix is one comment.

- A1 Test and entry names: the issue says `tests/ci-plan-reuse.bh-5354-test.sh` /

  `tests/harness-ci-reuse-shape.bh-5368-test.sh`; the entry keeps the issue's `BH-5354.2.md`. Other
  reading: name them bh-5354 (only the file names differ).
- A2 Token on the plan job: the issue says plan env `SUITE_LEDGER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUITE_LEDGER_TOKEN }}`
  and also "ordinary-PR jobs get no token". A `full`-labelled ordinary PR runs the plan job, so the token
  is gated to `push` or a merge-queue head ref. Other reading: unconditional secret (a full-label PR's
  code would hold the write token).
- A3 Eligibility: besides the `full` label and `unmapped:`, the batch escalation `member labels
  unreadable` also never looks up (it may be hiding a `full` label). Other reading: it looks up.
- A4 `CI_REUSE_CTX` uses `vars.CI_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"'` (the same default as `runs-on`) instead
  of bare `vars.CI_RUNNER`, because an empty ctx turns reuse off on a repo that never set the variable.
  Other reading: bare variable, reuse off until it is set.
- A5 Missing artifact on a shard: the issue says "unset, so --expect-n goes red". N is a ceiling of
